$comment: Accepted calls to the plan-ROW readers (getPlan / planLimits / planHasFeature), catalog indexes (recorded as the callee `PLANS[]`), comparisons that NAME A TIER in the source text (recorded as the callee `PlanId===`, both `===` and `!==`), and the deliberate leniency getEntitledPlanForIssuedGrant. See scripts/check-entitlement-gates.mjs, docs/billing.md and #476. Each entry states why this call is NOT a paid-feature gate resolved from the wrong question — or, for getEntitledPlanForIssuedGrant, which already-issued grant it continues, who holds it, and what bounds it. `arg` pins the source text of the first argument, or of the index expression for a `PLANS[]` entry: the reason is an argument about WHAT is passed, so the gate fails when that changes and the reason has to be re-argued. A key's middle segment is the enclosing function, or `METHOD /path` for an Express route handler in the dev server. `node scripts/check-entitlement-gates.mjs --print` prints a skeleton for every current finding. The list may only SHRINK: adding an entry admits new debt and needs the reason to hold up in review; a stale entry fails the gate so a fix must delete its line. `getEntitledPlan(sub)` is never a finding — it is the rule. A `PlanId===` entry states why naming that tier is NOT a paid-feature gate: a gate belongs on the `PlanFeatures` flag, read as `featureOf(getEntitledPlan(sub), flag)`, so a tier added between two existing ones is answered by its own row rather than by a literal that predates it (#592). Its `arg` is the whole comparison, operator included.

handlers/billing/handler.ts::checkoutSch.reason: Not entitlement, and not a capability. `v.planId` is the tier the request is asking to BUY, read out of the checkout body, and the refine asks whether a LIFETIME interval exists for it. That is a fact about the price catalogue — only Garden has a one-time SKU (`STRIPE_PRICE_ID_GARDEN_LIFETIME`) — not about what a tier includes once bought, which is why `PlanFeatures` has no flag for it. A tier added later is priced by adding its Stripe price ids, and this line is where that gets said.

Not entitlement. `v.planId` is the tier the request is asking to BUY, read out of the checkout body, and the refine only asks whether that tier still offers the requested billing interval (withdrawn cadences). There is no household subscription in scope at schema-validation time, and nothing here grants anything.

handlers/climate/moveDay.ts::evaluateMov.reason: CONTINUING. The grant is a claimed Move Day season: the list is already materialised as claimable tasks in the household's own task list and the card holds for MOVE_DAY_CARD_DAYS (14). Bounded by that window, and by Stripe resetting planId when dunning ends. Firing a NEW season three lines below uses getEntitledPlan, because claiming consumes the season for MOVE_DAY_REFIRE_GAP_DAYS (180) — a half-finished frost move is worse than either whole outcome.

handlers/plants/identify.ts::identify::g.reason: Not entitlement. A literal: the free tier's own row, used as the floor when the household has no entitlement. The entitled plan on this path is resolved by getEntitledPlan in the same expression (converted in #364).

handlers/tasks/handler.ts::getSitterBrie.reason: CONTINUING. The grant is a sitter link: issued while the household was entitled, carrying an `expiresAt`, and held by a sitter who is not the buyer and cannot fix a failed card. `sitterService.getActiveLink` has already enforced active + inside [startsAt, expiresAt] before this line, so an expired or revoked link never reaches it. Issuing a new link is gated on getEntitledPlan in handlers/households/handler.ts::createSitterLink.

handlers/tasks/handler.ts::getSitterView.reason: CONTINUING, same grant and same bounds as getSitterBrief above — this is the `briefAvailable` flag on the task view, and it must agree with the brief endpoint or the sitter page offers a control that then 404s. Same already-validated link.

handlers/tasks/sitterPhotos.ts::awayKitE.reason: CONTINUING, same grant and same bounds as the two sitter routes above. Both callers (getSitterPhotoStatus, uploadSitterPhoto) are the anonymous token routes, reached only after sitterService has validated an active, unexpired link. The photo-back cap is per-link and enforced separately.

local-server.ts::GET /sitter/:token/brie.reason: CONTINUING, dev server. Mirrors handlers/tasks/handler.ts::getSitterBrief above — same already-validated link, same bounds. The sitter holding it is not the buyer and cannot enter a payment method; the plants are what pay for a link that dies overnight.

local-server.ts::GET /sitter/:token::get.reason: CONTINUING, dev server. Mirrors handlers/tasks/handler.ts::getSitterView above: the `briefAvailable` flag on the anonymous sitter view. `getActiveSitterLink` has already enforced active + inside [startsAt, expiresAt] before this line, so an expired or revoked link never reaches it. It must agree with GET /sitter/:token/brief below, or the sitter page offers a control that then 404s. Issuing a NEW link is gated on getEntitledPlan in POST /households/:id/sitter-links.

local-server.ts::POST /households/:id/mo.reason: CONTINUING, dev server. Mirrors handlers/climate/moveDay.ts::evaluateMoveDay above: the grant is a claimed Move Day season, already materialised as claimable tasks in the household's own task list, with a 14-day card window bounding it. Firing a NEW season two lines below uses getEntitledPlan and answers 'quiet' rather than 'ready', so an unentitled household leaves the season UNCLAIMED instead of burning the 180-day re-fire gap.

local-server.ts::awayKitEnabledFor::getE.reason: CONTINUING, dev server. Mirrors handlers/tasks/sitterPhotos.ts::awayKitEnabledFor above. Both callers are the anonymous sitter photo routes (GET and POST /sitter/:token/photos), reached only after getActiveSitterLink validated the link; the per-link photo cap is enforced separately. The away RECAP deliberately does NOT call this — it is read by a signed-in member of the buying household and resolves through `entitledPlan`, exactly as handlers/households/awayRecap.ts does.

models/upgradeFeatures.ts::composeUpgrad.reason: Not entitlement. Names the TARGET tier in the email a member sends their admin (`input.targetPlanId`, already resolved by resolveTargetPlan). Copy, not a grant.
Not entitlement. Same target tier as the email above, for the push notification's copy.

models/upgradeFeatures.ts::resolveTarget.reason: Not a gate — the opposite, and the same function the getPlan entry below already covers. `id` iterates PLAN_ORDER looking for the lowest tier that RAISES the cap a member is asking for: an upsell target, not a grant. Newly listed because the gate now sees catalog indexing, not because this code changed.

Not a gate — tier ordering. This walks PLAN_ORDER for the cheapest tier that raises a cap, and excludes the FREE tier from being an upgrade TARGET; the ranking itself is `planRank`, and this clause only stops the search returning the floor it started above. A tier added later takes its place in PLAN_ORDER and is considered here with no edit. What is excluded is the free tier specifically, the one thing nobody upgrades to, and 'is the free tier' is not a capability a features flag could carry.

Not a gate — the opposite. Resolves which tier to UPSELL a household to given the tier it is on, and returns null when that tier already includes the feature. Reading the plan row is correct here: a household that already holds the tier must not be sold it again, whatever its payment status, which is the same rule services/billing.ts's double-pay guard enforces.

services/billing.ts::applyStripeEvent::P.reason: Not entitlement — analytics. Emits the activation product event only when the tier activated is a PAID one, so the free tier's own row is not counted as a conversion. Nothing is granted or refused here; access was decided upstream by getEntitledPlan. Any tier added later is paid unless it is the free floor, which is exactly what this names.

Not entitlement — analytics, the first-payment event. Same reason as the activation case above: a transition into `active` on the free tier is not a payment, so the free tier is excluded from the count. It grants nothing.
Not entitlement — analytics, the churn event. Losing the free tier is not churn, so the free tier is excluded from the count. It revokes nothing; the downgrade itself is applied by the delta above.

services/billing.ts::createCheckoutSessi.reason: Not entitlement. `args.planId` is the tier being PURCHASED, used to look up its Stripe price and cadence. Nothing is granted here; the grant arrives on the webhook.

Not entitlement. Names the lifetime tier a household ALREADY owns in the LIFETIME_ALREADY_OWNED refusal message. This is the double-pay guard refusing a second sale, so reading the owned row is exactly right — a lifetime purchase is a floor no status may fall below.

services/billingEmailCopy.ts::cancellati.reason: Not entitlement. A literal: the free tier's NAME, so the cancellation email can say which tier the household will land on.

services/billingEmailCopy.ts::itemLabel:.reason: Not entitlement. A tier NAME for one line item on an invoice email. The item is a record of what was billed, not a decision about what may be used.
Not entitlement. The other branch of the same invoice line-item label.

services/billingEmails.ts::readHousehold.reason: Not entitlement. Resolves the tier NAME for billing email copy. A FAILED read never reaches this line (the send throws); a missing attribute correctly renders the free tier's name. Nothing is granted from it.

services/escalation.ts::runEscalations::.reason: Not a plan-row read. `rule.planId` is ALREADY the entitled plan id: getEscalationRule resolves it through getEntitledPlan from the same projected GetItem (planId + subscriptionStatus + lifetimePlanId), so this is a catalog lookup on a resolved id. Delete this line if that resolution ever moves back to the row.

services/sitterPlanGate.ts::checkSitterL.reason: Not the gate — the MESSAGE. The gate is the two caps read immediately above (`plan.limits.sitterLinkMaxDays`, `plan.limits.sitterLinksActive`); this only chooses whether the refusal sentence names Garden as the lift or says 'Shorten the window'. A tier added between Seedling and Garden would therefore get a slightly wrong upsell sentence, not free access. If that copy ever needs to be exact, the right answer is `resolveTargetPlan` (models/upgradeFeatures.ts), which computes the real upgrade target, not another literal.

services/stripePrices.ts::expectedPriceF.reason: Not entitlement. `planId` is a PlanId parameter naming which catalog row to read the expected Stripe amounts from, so the price-drift check can compare the catalog against the live Price objects. No household is in scope — the function takes a tier and a cadence and returns a price row. Newly listed because the gate now sees catalog indexing, not because this code changed.
